# **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – no standardised first-touch-to-first-class journey; likely inconsistent conversion and retention impact
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no documented win-back or exit interview process; losing data on why members leave
- **Member Pause** – no clear criteria, duration limits, or re-engagement trigger; probably ad-hoc decisions
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – no progression path for coaches; affects retention and quality consistency

# Service Menu Creation — Action Plan for Grace

• **Split into two separate documents immediately.** Coaches need internal specs (what they're selling, margin structure, upsell triggers). Members see only benefits, pricing, and what's included. Use Canva template or Google Docs — don't overthink format. This isn't marketing collateral yet.

• **Price anchor backwards from your revenue target.** How much per month does The Forge need per active member to hit profit? Lock that number first, then build tiers around it. Most gym owners price what competitors charge — Grace should price what she *needs*. Example: if you need £40/week revenue per member, a monthly tier is £160-180, not £99.

• **Stack 3 tiers minimum: basic (studio classes only), standard (classes + coach access 2x/month), premium (unlimited coach time + nutrition checkin).** Make standard the obvious middle choice — that's where 60% of your members will land. Price premium aggressively; it's your profit centre.

• **For coaches: attach specific service descriptions to each tier.** "Premium member = 15-min form check-in per session, 1:1 program tweak monthly." Vague services = scope creep = resentment. Your coaches need to know exactly what they're delivering at each price point.

• **Lock this in writing this week, share with team for feedback, live by end of next week.** Ambiguity kills sales conversations. Your team needs to sell this with conviction.

What's your current pricing structure? That'll tell me if Grace is leaving money on the table.
